priorStories.headline: U.S. military disables cargo ship near Iran
priorStories.body:
U.S. Central Command said an American military aircraft disabled a St. Kitts-flagged commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday after its crew ignored repeated warnings and tried to breach the U.S. blockade of Iran.

The vessel was leaving regional waters after visiting an Iranian port, the command said. Reuters identified it as the M/V Huda and reported that precision munitions struck its stern after the crew was directed to leave the targeted areas.

candidates.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said on November 8 that it intercepted two ballistic missiles directed toward Riyadh, another toward the Eastern Province, and two cruise missiles over Riyadh and the southern region. A Reuters witness heard booms after a civil-defense alert in Riyadh; authorities subsequently issued an all-clear. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said falling debris caused minor damage to an Aramco building in Riyadh, with no casualties reported.
candidates.title: Saudi coalition reports missile interceptions; ministry reports debris damage to Aramco building

sources.name: Associated Press via The Washington Post

candidates.summary: The Russian-installed management of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant reported on November 8 that the plant had lost external electricity after protective systems disconnected the damaged Ferosplavna line. Management said backup diesel generators were supplying equipment needed for safe operation and radiation readings remained normal. The statement did not identify the cause of the damage.
candidates.title: Zaporizhzhia plant management reports loss of external power

candidates.summary: Ukrainian authorities said a Russian drone struck emergency workers conducting rescue operations in Komyshuvakha on November 8. Ukraine's State Emergency Service reported no injuries but said specialized rescue equipment was damaged. The location, including a former school and nearby shelter, had been struck by guided bombs on November 2; the Sunday drone strike was a separate development.
candidates.title: Ukraine reports drone strike on rescuers at Komyshuvakha disaster site

candidates.summary: Polish prosecutors said on November 8 they had opened an investigation into murder and attempted murder, including attacks on police officers, treating the previous day's Krakow shooting as a terrorist offense. Police identified three people found dead at the suspect's family home as his sister and parents, saying they likely died from gunshot wounds. Saturday's Main Square attack killed six people and wounded 15 others. The suspect remained hospitalized.
candidates.title: Polish prosecutors announce terrorism-related investigation into Krakow shooting

candidates.summary: Two passenger trains collided in Egypt's Giza province on November 8, killing at least four people and injuring 88, the health ministry said. The railway authority said a train traveling from Giza to Fayoum struck the rear of a Cairo-to-Aswan train, derailing carriages. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi ordered an investigation. Emergency crews were clearing wreckage to restore services on the Cairo–Upper Egypt line.
candidates.title: Egypt reports four killed and 88 injured in passenger-train collision

candidates.summary: President Isaac Herzog formally gave Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to try to form Israel's next government at a November 8 ceremony. Eisenkot called for a national emergency government and said Likud and the Religious Zionist Party could support a government under his leadership. He received recommendations from parties representing 67 lawmakers during presidential consultations, compared with 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu. Those recommendations do not establish that a governing coalition has been formed.
candidates.title: Herzog formally tasks Eisenkot with forming Israel's next government

candidates.summary: Iran's judiciary said Hassan Divband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were executed on the morning of November 8 after the Supreme Court upheld their death sentences. The judiciary accused them of conducting operations for Israel, the United States and hostile groups during January anti-government protests, including armed attacks and arson in Karaj. These allegations are the judiciary's account, not independently established findings.
candidates.title: Iran announces executions of three men convicted over January protests

candidates.summary: Polish prosecutors opened a November 8 investigation treating the previous day's Krakow shooting, which killed six people, as a terrorist offense. The investigation also covers the November 7 killings of the suspect's parents and sister in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski; prosecutors said evidence indicated the same person committed both attacks. The suspect remained hospitalized in critical condition and had not been formally detained because of his medical condition, officials told ABC News. Poland began two days of national mourning. Reports differed on the number injured.
candidates.title: Polish prosecutors link Krakow terrorism investigation to three family killings

candidates.summary: In November 8 television interviews, Representative Robert Garcia said prospective Democratic congressional investigations would focus on Elon Musk's involvement in federal workforce cuts and Stephen Miller's role in immigration enforcement. Hakeem Jeffries said he would support a proposed impeachment measure against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the administration was prepared to oppose such efforts. These were statements of intent and support, not announcements of opened investigations or an impeachment vote.
candidates.title: Democratic lawmakers outline oversight plans; Jeffries backs proposed Hegseth impeachment

The vessel was leaving regional waters after visiting an Iranian port, the command said. Reuters identified it as the M/V Huda and reported that precision munitions struck its stern after the crew was directed to leave the targeted areas.

candidates.summary: Egyptian authorities raised the toll from the November 8 passenger-train collision in al-Ayyat, Giza province, to seven dead and at least 125 injured. The Health Ministry said more than 70 injured people had been discharged after treatment. Prosecutors said an initial inspection indicated that the Giza–Fayoum train struck the last carriage of a stationary Cairo–Aswan train on the same track. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi ordered an investigation.
candidates.title: Egypt train-collision toll rises to seven dead and at least 125 injured

candidates.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed on November 8 that Ukraine's Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant lost off-site electricity after the Ferosplavna power line disconnected and was using emergency diesel generators for cooling. The agency said the cause and location of the disconnection were not yet known and estimated that fuel reserves could support a limited number of generators for about two weeks. Russian-installed plant management reported normal radiation readings.
candidates.title: IAEA confirms Zaporizhzhia power loss and use of emergency generators

candidates.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Buenos Aires from Uruguay on November 8 and met Argentine President Javier Milei. In his first public address in Argentina, Leo told officials, diplomats and civic leaders that economic policy should serve people. His remarks addressed governance, social justice and artificial intelligence against the backdrop of Milei's austerity program.
candidates.title: Pope Leo arrives in Argentina and urges people-centered economic policy

candidates.summary: In a November 8 CNN interview, President Donald Trump said renewed U.S. attacks on Iran were unlikely to be necessary if Tehran signed a strong agreement, while retaining the option of military action. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi separately told state television that mediators had stopped traveling following the U.S. midterm elections. In a Sunday social-media statement, Araghchi said Iran's existing two-day proposal remained available, conditional on its requirements being met. The statements did not announce an agreement or a resumption of negotiations.
candidates.title: Trump discusses conditional restraint on Iran as Araghchi reports pause in mediator travel

candidates.summary: Nvidia's board announced on November 8 an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Its statement said independent directors assisted by outside counsel would oversee the review. The board said it had no reason to believe that U.S. national security or company secrets had been compromised, expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team, and said Huang supported the investigation and would cooperate. The announcement did not establish the underlying espionage allegations.
candidates.title: Nvidia board announces independent review of reported intelligence targeting of Huang
